answer: Latency-Weighted Attention Ledger. Each identity accumulates credit only by responding to randomly timed micro-tasks within a tight window; credit decays unless refreshed at unpredictable intervals, so maintaining N identities requires N concurrent attentive operators, not scripts. Attackers must pay for parallel human attention, like keeping a reef alive through constant tending. A zephyr of idle automation earns nothing because responses arrive too fast or too uniform. Cost scales linearly with identity count and cannot be amortized across a juniper-thin budget of shared staff,
